title: Beyond the Byline
subtitle: Listening outranks the personal triumph of getting a story
sourceCredit: Dinesh Ramde · The Moth Radio Hour, “Acceptance”

shot.title: A large name on the page
shot.direction: The reporter’s byline dominates; the subject’s life is only an empty white box.
shot.soundDirection: Newsroom typewriter, interrupted dial tone, soft conversational silence.

illustration.direction: The reporter sits at a modest work desk, a notebook open under his naturally held pen and a telephone within reach. His face shows ambition and pleased anticipation as he looks at his own drafted page. An oversized plain header block fills much of the notebook while a pale empty rectangular window beyond the telephone suggests the not-yet-seen source's life. No readable byline, headline or real newspaper branding; paper proportions and his attention carry the imbalance.

shot.title: The line goes quiet
shot.direction: The receiver stills. The blank rectangle occupies more of the page.

beats.caption: This could be the story everyone reads.

shot.title: The hoped-for headline
shot.direction: The reporter begins from ambition and his own drafted words. After the line, the pen pauses and a small shift of attention prepares the telephone pickup without a premature listening pose.

actions.direction: His pen pauses after the ambitious line; a small shift of attention prepares the connected receiver pickup in the next cutaway.

beats.caption: Are you listening to what this costs me?
beats.speaker: SOURCE

shot.title: The human cost
shot.direction: A brief connected hand-and-receiver close-up carries the pickup into the listening view. The receiver and head settle before the source’s question begins; the conversation remains connected in all later views.
shot.soundDirection: Newsroom typewriter, interrupted dial tone, soft conversational silence.

illustration.direction: The reporter has picked up the receiver in one hand while the pen in his other hovers just above the notebook without moving. His brows lift as he listens, mouth no longer forming his own line. The pale rectangular space beyond the phone grows more prominent but remains indistinct, with only a faint suggestion of an ordinary chair. Keep wrist, pen grip, telephone contact and chair support physically credible. The speaker's life is not yet filled with invented details.

actions.direction: The lifted receiver settles against the ear before the caller speaks. Head and held receiver make a small connected final adjustment, then the shoulders release.

shot.title: The pen stops
shot.direction: The pen is released onto the notebook as the same connected call continues. Give the uncomfortable realization a brief visible hand action before his answer, without restoring the receiver to its cradle.
shot.soundDirection: Newsroom typewriter, interrupted dial tone, soft conversational silence.

illustration.direction: The reporter sets his pen down flat on the notebook, fingers visibly releasing it, and turns his attention away from the oversized header block. In a clearly separate softly edged room-space at the other side of the wide cell, the source sits in a plain chair with her own receiver, wary but direct. Only a small table, cup and curtain establish ordinary life; no documents or photos suggest an invented backstory. His face registers uncomfortable self-recognition. The reporter continues holding his own receiver to his left ear while his right fingers release the pen; his phone base has an empty cradle and the two rooms remain distinct.

actions.direction: His fingers withdraw a fraction from the pen, followed by a small chin dip. The pen, notebook and phone base stay fixed. The separate caller is not moved by his action.

beats.caption: I was hearing my own headline.
beats.speaker: REPORTER

shot.title: Hearing himself
shot.direction: He recognizes that he had been listening for his headline.

shot.title: The chair turns
shot.direction: A clean brief change of view gives the reporter’s turned attention to the caller. Keep the receiver at his ear; let the caller’s next sentence follow the settling posture promptly.
shot.soundDirection: Newsroom typewriter, interrupted dial tone, soft conversational silence.

illustration.direction: The reporter swivels his actual chair slightly away from the desk, notebook and pen left undisturbed behind his forearm, while he listens on the phone. The source's separate room now occupies an equal portion of the illustration, its simple chair, side table, cup and window softly present. Both are fully recognizable and physically grounded in their own spaces; no shared desk or invented in-person meeting is implied. His body now faces her visual space instead of his page.

shot.title: Start again
shot.direction: The subject begins again. Ordinary life details enter the formerly blank panel.
shot.soundDirection: Newsroom typewriter, interrupted dial tone, soft conversational silence.

illustration.direction: The source's ordinary room takes more of the wide frame. She sits supported in her chair, holds her receiver securely with one hand and offers a small open palm with the other as she begins again. Her face is measured and serious, not a staged tragic expression. In the smaller separate reporter space he listens with his pen still flat on the page. Keep room details modest and nonbiographical; no painted story, family history or personal crisis is added.

actions.direction: The caller makes one contained hand offer while the hand holding the receiver stays in contact. The listener inclines his head later; the gutter keeps their physical spaces separate.

shot.title: Listening now
shot.direction: The reporter does not write through this answer; his attention remains on the person.
shot.soundDirection: Newsroom typewriter, interrupted dial tone, soft conversational silence.

illustration.direction: The source and her quiet domestic space occupy most of the illustration, warm natural light on her attentive face and ordinary furnishings. The reporter remains visibly separate at the far side, phone held naturally, gaze lifted, notebook with a now-small blank header block resting on his desk and pen untouched. Both people have equal human scale even though her environment has visual priority. No published scoop, award, triumphant handshake or new story text closes the scene.

actions.direction: The writer’s head gives one small acknowledgment; his receiver and hand stay together. The caller’s hand rests. The motion ends before the next line can feel prompted.

shot.title: Life fills the page
shot.direction: The subject’s ordinary room has visual priority now. Leave a quiet listening space after the short exchange, with slight curtain and body motion, rather than separating the spoken replies with long dead air.
